study: Augsburg Confession Articles IV/V/X in Invariata and Variata
method: Keep edition wording, theological interpretation, and reception history distinct

questions.continuity: Both present forgiveness/justification through Christ and faith rather than human merit.
questions.revision: 1540 develops a longer exposition of gospel promise, repentance, assurance and Christian consolation.
questions.interpretation_risk: Do not equate expanded description with complete replacement of justification doctrine.

questions.continuity: Gospel ministry, Word, sacraments, and the work of the Holy Spirit connect to faith.
questions.revision: Historical editors identify expanded formulations and differences regarding means of grace, including omission of 'ubi et quando visum est Deo' in 1540.
questions.interpretation_risk: Whether formulation changed the doctrine is contested; distinguish actual omission from confessional assessment.

questions.continuity: Both confess Christ's body and blood in connection with the Lord's Supper.
questions.revision: 1530: vere adsint et distribuantur; 1540: cum pane et vino vere exhibeantur; latter omits express rejection of differently teaching views.
questions.interpretation_risk: Reception by Lutheran and Reformed writers differed; 'exhibeantur' does not alone prove a single settled Calvinist doctrine.

connections.relationship: justification and means through which faith is given
sacraments as means of grace and specific claim about Lord's Supper
shared confession but distinct controversies; justification and presence should not be collapsed

reception_positions.position: 1540 changes raised later concerns about Eucharistic teaching and Article V phrasing
1540 sought compromise and clearer common ground, yet was not universally received; Melanchthon's intention should not be collapsed to Zwinglian memorialism
